Extremely Disappointing – Poorly Managed & Ruined My Birthday

I booked an appointment five days in advance for both hair and nails, specifically to prepare for my birthday. I expected a relaxing, professional experience—but instead, I left feeling stressed, angry, and completely disappointed.

When I arrived, the salon was overbooked. They started doing my nails in a random area that clearly wasn’t meant for nails—honestly, I don’t even know what that space was. It was uncomfortable and unprofessional. I had to ask to be moved to a proper station.

After finishing my nails, I was left standing with no waiting area, waiting to be called for my hair. When they finally washed my hair, they left me sitting with wet hair down my back for 15–20, no explanation. I had to get up and speak to someone myself.

One of the staff members tried to explain, and I could tell she was doing her best. But the real issue is poor management. There are three receptionists, yet no one is handling appointments properly. What’s the point of having a team at the front desk if everything is unorganized?

I pay to come here and feel good, not to leave stressed and angry. If you're overbooked, just say so. I booked early, especially for a special occasion, and I would’ve gone somewhere else if I had known.

Poor hygiene
No proper waiting or sitting area
They charge for coffee and water, which is fine—but at least provide a clean, relaxing space to enjoy it
This was supposed to be a treat for myself on my birthday. Instead, it turned into a stressful experience. I sincerely hope management takes this seriously. This is not the kind of service anyone should pay for.Never again.

text:
Bedashing used to be my absolute go-to salon for everything beauty-related. I genuinely loved going there.

Recently, I went in for hair coloring and a botox hair treatment. The service itself was fine, and I was clear from the beginning about exactly what I wanted.

However, what disappointed me was the way additional services were handled. When it was time to sign the bill, I was surprised to see that two “hair heat protectant” treatments had been added — without my knowledge or consent. I was told it was necessary to prevent my hair and scalp from burning. If it was truly essential, that should have been clearly explained beforehand.

Each application cost 330 AED — meaning I paid 660 AED for something I never agreed to, almost the same price as the hair coloring itself. At that point, I felt uncomfortable questioning it, so I signed the bill — but that doesn’t make it right.

Unfortunately, it didn’t stop there. At the cashier, I was presented with a full set of Kerastase products to purchase. When I declined, I was told, “Your hairdresser said you will buy it.” I refused again and explained that I had never agreed to purchase anything. While products were mentioned during the service, it was clearly promotional — at no point did I commit to buying them.

This experience left me feeling pressured and misled. I understand upselling is part of business, but adding services without consent and assuming product purchases crosses a line.

It’s really disappointing because Bedashing was once my favorite salon. Sadly, this will be my last visit. I don’t tolerate feeling taken advantage of, especially from a brand of this size and reputation.

If you never read a review before, I suggest that you seek this one out. I hardly ever write reviews, in fact, I can't even remember the last time I did. But this time is really different because of the services I received.

Bedashing Beauty Lounge isn't new to me; I've been there twice before, but this time was a true letdown. The staff there were quite unpleasant, but let's not dwell on that as everyone has their days; let's focus on the services I received.

I'm an expert when it comes to blowouts at different salons, so I can tell the difference between a good one and a bad one. I initially asked for a blowout, which usually includes curling the ends of your hair, right? Wrong.
The lady sat me down, offered me drinks without mentioning they were chargeable. Naturally, I assumed they were complimentary. I had to ask her to find out they were not.

I requested the ends to be pinned up, assuming she would do it as part of the blowout, but she agreed with some hesitation, which felt strange. She didn't even ask me about my preferred hair parting; I had to tell her I wanted a middle part. She then incorrectly sectioned the middle part and pinned my bangs the wrong way, neglecting my baby hair.

When I went to pay, I was shocked at the price! Can you believe they charged extra for the curls at the end of the blowout? 50 dirhams extra that she didn't even inform me about! On top of the blowout charge that already costed 150dirhams so now the total is 200 that I did not even know I was paying for I wouldn’t have minded if I only knew about it.

I will not be visiting again, and I suggest that anyone who goes there ask about the price of everything, as they will not inform you and will hide it until you go to pay at the checkout. What a waste of a beautifully decorated salon with horrible service. You are supposed to leave feeling good about your self but I left with a bitter taste about it all.

Also the hair barely lasted a day, on top of the bad services, their work does not even stay, she did not even spray my hair with hairspray. It is a crime to charge this much for on a service that does not even remain.

I am extremely disappointed with my experience at the Khalifa Branch.

On Friday, 07/08/2026, I purchased RevitaLash from the branch specifically for my eyelashes. Before purchasing it, I clearly asked the staff member who was assisting me whether the product was for eyelashes, and she confirmed that it was.

When I arrived home and opened the product, I discovered that it was actually for eyebrows, not eyelashes. I contacted the branch immediately on the same day to report the issue, but no one followed up with me.

The following day, I contacted the branch again. I was told that I had called early in the morning and that they had only just started their shift and had not yet found a solution. Later, I was asked to send photos of the product, which I did immediately. However, once again, no one followed up with me, and I had to keep sending messages myself to get an update.

I only received a proper response on Tuesday, several days after I first reported the issue. I was then informed that because I had opened the product, they would not refund me. I explained that I only opened it because I had been specifically assured by their staff that it was the correct product for eyelashes.

What disappointed me even more was the way the situation was handled. I was told that the mistake was not theirs, that I should have read the product myself before opening it, and that they had given me the correct product. I was also told, “I am not saying that you are lying, but we gave you the correct product.”

I find this response completely unacceptable and unprofessional. As a customer, I relied on the advice and confirmation of the staff member who was assisting me. If I had been given the correct information in the first place, I would never have purchased or opened the wrong product.

My complaint is therefore not only about receiving the wrong product. It is also about the lack of follow-up, the way responsibility was placed entirely on me despite the incorrect advice given by the staff, and most importantly, the inappropriate way the matter was communicated to me.

I expected the branch management to handle my complaint professionally and take responsibility for the customer service provided by their staff, rather than making me feel as though I was at fault or that my explanation was being questioned.

I am requesting that this complaint be reviewed seriously and that an appropriate resolution be provided.

لأن فرع شخبوط كان مسكر، رحت فرع خليفة. وللأسف ضيعت أكثر من خمس ساعات من يومي، غير المبلغ اللي دفعته، ولو شارية فيه ذهب كان أبرك.

للأسف النتيجة كانت سيئة، لكن الأسوأ كان أسلوب التعامل. كل اللي سألته بكل احترام هو: هل كان ممكن تكون النتيجة أفضل؟ أو فيه طريقة نعدلها بدون ما نحرق الشعر؟

المشكلة كانت واضحة، الجهة اليسرى غير الجهة اليمنى. أنا أصلًا كنت راضية عن الجهة اليسرى، لكن اليمنى كانت سيئة. أنا ما كنت طالبة شعر ستريت، وكل اللي قصدته إنه لو الكوافيرة السورية أعادت تمرير البيبي ليس مرة ثانية مع شد بسيط على الجهة اليمنى كان ممكن تتحسن النتيجة.

بدل ما تجاوب على سؤالي، زعلت وبدأت تدافع عن نفسها، وجابت أكثر من موظفة من الصالون. حتى الكوافيرة السينيور المصرية اللي شعرها مصبوغ أشقر دخلت في النقاش، مع إنها أصلًا ما كانت شايفة شعري ولا تعرف شو كان طلبي، ومع ذلك أصرت أن الحل الوحيد هو البروتين. من كثر ما تجمعوا علي وكل وحدة تتكلم، ما قدرت حتى أوضح وجهة نظري أو أشرح المشكلة اللي كنت أقصدها .. وانا مسويه البروداكت هذا ألف مره فعارفه كيف المفروض تكون النتيجة.

والأكثر إحراجًا أنهم ناقشوا الموضوع كله قدام الزبائن، والكوافيرة صارت توصف شعري كيف كان وكيف صار، ووصفها أصلًا كان غير صحيح، مع أني ما طلبت منها تشرح أو تبرر لأحد.

كذلك قصت لي شعري، ومع أنها غسلت شعري مرتين وجففته مرتين، ما انتبهت أن الطول غير متساوٍ. نبهتها أكثر من مرة، لكنها بعد القص ورّتني صورة للشعر وقالت إنه متساوٍ، ولأن الصورة ما كانت مبينة جوانب الشعر بشكل واضح شككت في نفسي واقتنعت بكلامها. وبعدها اكتشفت أن الصورة أصلًا ما كانت تبين الجوانب لأنها كانت داخلة، بينما الواقع أن الجوانب كانت قبل القص أقصر من الشعر اللي في الوسط، وبعد القص ما ساوتهم، فصاروا أطول من الشعر اللي بالنص.

حتى بعد الصبغة، طلبت بكل أدب قطعة قطن مع مزيل الصبغة عشان أمسح وجهي، فقامت تبرر لي ليش وجهي متلطخ بالصبغة. قلت لها: أنا ما سألتك ليش، أنا فقط طلبت قطن. فقالت: عشان لا تقولين ليش. مع أني أصلًا ما سألت عن السبب.

طلعت من الصالون وأنا حاسة أني ارتكبت جريمة فقط لأني سألت إذا كان بالإمكان تكون النتيجة أفضل. للأسف ما كان فيه أي تقبل للملاحظة أو محاولة لفهم العميل، وكل اللي شفته كان دفاع مستمر عن الخطأ.

وهذه للأسف أسوأ تجربة مررت فيها مع أي صالون. والأغرب أني من عملاء هذا المكان من أول ما تأسس، لذلك مستغربة جدًا كيف وصل مستوى الخدمة والتعامل إلى هذا الحد. وين المالكة القديمة وين أيامها

Because the Shakhbout branch was closed, I went to the Khalifa branch. Unfortunately, I wasted more than five hours of my day, not to mention the money I paid—I would have been better off buying gold with that money.

Unfortunately, the result was bad, but what was worse was the way I was treated. All I asked, respectfully, was: Could the result have been better? Or is there a way to fix it without damaging my hair?

The problem was obvious: the left side was different from the right. I was actually happy with the left side, but the right one was awful. I wasn't asking for straight hair; all I meant was that if the Syrian hairdresser had gone over the right side with the flat iron a second time, with a little more tension, the result might have been better.

Instead of answering my question, she got upset and started defending herself, bringing in several other employees from the salon. Even the senior Egyptian hairdresser with blonde hair joined the discussion, even though she hadn't seen my hair or known what I wanted. Despite that, she insisted that the only solution was a protein treatment. Because so many people crowded around me, each one talking, I couldn't even explain my point of view or clarify the problem I was referring to. I've done this product a thousand times, so I know what the result should be.

What was even more embarrassing was that they discussed the whole thing in front of the customers. The hairdresser started describing how my hair was before and how it was now, and her description was completely inaccurate, even though I hadn't asked her to explain or justify anything to anyone.

She also cut my hair, and even though she washed and dried it twice, she didn't notice that the lengths were uneven. I pointed this out to her several times, but after the cut, she showed me a picture of my hair and said it was even. Because the picture didn't clearly show the sides, I doubted myself and believed her. Later, I discovered that the picture didn't show the sides because they were hidden inside. In reality, the sides were shorter than the hair in the middle before the cut, and after the cut, they weren't evened out, so they ended up longer than the hair in the middle.

Even after the dyeing, I politely asked for a cotton pad with dye remover to wipe my face. She then started explaining why my face was stained with dye. I told her, "I didn't ask why; I just asked for cotton." She replied, "So you wouldn't ask why." Even though I hadn't asked the reason in the first place.

I left the salon feeling like I'd committed a crime simply for asking if the result could be better. Unfortunately, there was absolutely no acceptance of feedback or attempt to understand the client; all I saw was a constant defense of the mistake.

This is, unfortunately, the worst experience I've ever had with any salon. What's even stranger is that I've been a customer since it first opened, so I'm very surprised how the service and treatment have deteriorated to this level. Where is the old owner? Where are those days?

text:
I have been a loyal customer of Bedashing since its inception, and it was once one of the best nail salons in Abu Dhabi. Unfortunately, the level of service at this branch has significantly declined and has become extremely disappointing.

On more than five occasions, I specifically booked hair services with a particular technician (Lycil) at a confirmed time, only to arrive on time — and often even early — and still be left waiting for over 30 minutes. What is even more frustrating is seeing the same technician begin servicing another client instead of honoring my confirmed appointment. This reflects a complete lack of respect for customers’ time and poor appointment management.

What makes this worse is that raising these concerns with branch management (Julie and Fatima) has resulted in no meaningful action or improvement.

I am also extremely concerned about the integrity of the hair treatments being provided. After receiving a BB Crème treatment, sulfate-containing shampoo was used despite this treatment specifically requiring sulfate-free products to maintain results. This caused the treatment to wear off prematurely. When I raised this issue last year, the branch redid the treatment free of charge — which only confirmed that the mistake should never have happened in the first place. To be clear, the same technician is the one who used sulfate shampoo on my hair again, leaving no room to dismiss this as an innocent oversight.

That said, I would like to acknowledge Retchel, Lalin, and Milarose, who consistently provide excellent nail service and demonstrate professionalism that reflects the standards Bedashing was once known for.

It is disappointing to see such a reputable brand fall short at this branch. I strongly urge higher management to step in, investigate these recurring issues, and restore the quality, professionalism, and customer care that loyal clients have come to expect from Bedashing.

reviewContext/Stylist:
I came in already showered and dryed my hair, my hair is curly.

The stylist didn’t brush my hair or bother to wet it.

She wanted to cut it dry + keep in mind my hair is not straight + she did not brush it.

She divided it with a hair clip rather than a proper hair brush and it hurt cuz my hair was getting stuck in the clip.

I politely asked: are you going to cut my hair like that? (I get my hair trim every month so I know how it should be cut)

She said yes - no need for wetting it. I asked her to spray some water on it she kept insisting that it does need to and that would be a (Cut Style) I asked what’s a Cut Style? Maybe I need to pay more for wetting hair? IDK

She proceeded to cut I said please at least wet it (with a water spray) because I don’t want my hair to be uneven.

She said your hair is already not even (her voice was getting louder) - & I know my hair is even especially that i get it cut straight every month (the proper way).

Again i asked her to wet it she raised her hands ✋🏻 ✋🏻 at me mid of my talking.
Then she took a big water sprayer and kept spritzing on my head.

I did not react - I let her cut it. it was a trim and I stayed silent until she was done. She said do you want anything else? I just left without responding, to the reception.

The reception vibe was off and it seemed everyone was pressured, they want to close maybe at 8:00pm? (Even though that is not their closing time)

Anyway I paid and left.

I went there to feel better about myself and I left feeling bad and disrespected.

I mean if you can wet my hair and you have a water sprayer hair why negotiate it from the beginning?

Staff should be trained how to deal with customers. We are also moms/employees/whatever… when we decide to go to a salon we expect a service at a certain level - this is definitely not the level I was expecting from this salon, especially that I have been a customer for years.

text:
Wow, wow, the negative reviews definitely mirror my experience. Went to this salon in nad al Sheba for the first time. I’ll explain chronologically.
1.) I enter the salon and am being brought to the hair styling section. The receptionist is asking me where I’d like to sit, I could choose any seat. Before I had the chance to say anything the “hair stylist” decided where I have to sit.
2.) important for later: Being seated there, I directly shared that I am currently recovering from an upper body surgery.
3.) When she started washing my hair she asked me if the water temp. is ok. I told that she could make it warmer please. Her reply was an unfriendly “will be later”. Then why do u ask about the temperature if u can’t change it anyways? It can’t get colder than this and if it’s not in your hands to make it warmer, don’t ask. Tell from the beginning that we have to wait a bit.
4.) during the hair wash she was extremely rough and half of my face got wet which I had to tell her. Furthermore she asked me where to put the conditioner in my hair?!  I expect an expert to know where to put conditioner….
5.) when she put the “towel” (they only use disposable papers), my entire back got wet cause she wasn’t able to put the “towel” properly on my head. Mind you I have an upper body surgery and especially now no water must reach that part of the body. When I told her that she started discussing with me that nothing is wet 😅 she rolled her eyes looking at a colleague after this, which is clearly unacceptable.
6.) I had to request another hair stylist because I didn’t feel comfortable and treated with experience at all anymore. I even said I will wait until the other expert has finished but I was told the other lady can’t do at all because she has clients booked in her agenda. I understood this and said then - to make this whole nightmare end - I just need someone to dry the dripping wet hair so I can leave. I was told that an assistant (no qualified hair stylist personnel) could help with that but I would have to pay AED 90. Because I’m using the service 😂 for me it’s not about the money cause I initially came for a blow dry styling which is about double the price. But being so harsh to request 90 dirhams despite all that has happened is really not service & customer oriented. I requested them to call the manager and luckily we got to the agreement that I will get the dripping wet hair dried and don’t have to pay. However, even the manager was still trying to ensure that I don’t get the styling at all (as I won’t pay).
7.) later on the chair the assistant started to dry my hair but didn’t use any hair brush or comb to detangle. I was told this is not feasible cause she doesn’t know how to do it. Sorry, she doesn’t know how to comb hair?! I how does she comb her own every day? I was shocked about this level of unprofessionalism. I had to remind her 2x to use a brush - not for styling! Just to detangle!! -  and the second time she refused saying there is no brush left someone else would’ve taken it 😂 imagine, in the entire salon she wants to make me believe there is only 1 brush. After me pushing on this topic, she asked someone for permission to get a brush. I unfortunately cannot recommend this salon and the other experiences only second what I have faced today. Wish it had been different.

I advise against going to this place for massages at all, and I also advise against using their hair services because they are not worth the effort. I suggest no one should bother coming for a massage here.

Regarding nails; I asked for quick-drying nail polish drops, but the employee rushed the application, causing the polish, which should have been left to dry for ten minutes, to shrink. This resulted in marks and bumps instead of drying properly. Also, the treatment prices are exorbitant, and the service is very basic; you won't notice any difference.

textTranslated:
My experience was below expectations, and I'd give it less than one star.

Based on the praise I'd read, I thought this was the best salon that would pamper me and take care of my hair, but I was wrong.

The place wasn't clean when I arrived. There was cotton on the floor, red nail polish, and some of the chairs were stained.

The employee started suggesting the most expensive treatment, and when I chose the slightly cheaper one, she told me it wouldn't work and wouldn't show any effect on my hair.

While she was doing my hair, she chewed gum in an unpleasant way and seemed very rushed, as if she had something else to do, even though the hair section was empty and there was only one customer in the nail section.

The hospitality wasn't like other salons, and the scalp massage wasn't what I'm used to.

It was like I'd washed my hair and applied a hair mask at home.

I've tried Red Door, Miss Caramel, Rashna, and Lulu Glam, and they all take good care of the customer. And at her leisure.

Even while the woman was drying my hair, she seemed so annoyed that I was embarrassed my hair wasn't drying quickly.

When she got the comb, she pulled my hair so hard I felt it breaking. Every time I told her, "Please, reduce the heat of the blow dryer; it's burning me," she'd lower it a little, then increase it again when she sensed I wasn't paying attention.

As I was leaving, the employee asked me after I paid, "How was your experience?" I smiled and left.

At all the salons I mentioned, I leave with my hair looking better and cleaner than here. I wasn't even comfortable; the chairs were uncomfortable.

For the same price, I get a hair treatment with fresh ingredients, a massage, steam, a blow-dry, and a hair serum at other salons.

An experience I won't repeat.

The Kerastase  treatment was fine, and the technician was respectful and friendly — but unfortunately, that is the only positive comment I can give.

The blow dry experience was disappointing and barely acceptable for the price paid. I clearly requested a blow dry only (plus treatment), asking for straight hair with just some movement at the ends (which the technician confirmed), and for the iron to be used only on my half roots in the front and baby hairs near the ears. Instead, the stylist did more of a dry than a proper blow dry, leaving my hair frizzy and not smoothed out, then unexpectedly started using a curling iron I never asked for. Even after repeating the blow dry(as per my request), my roots were not straightened, and the end result was curly rather than straight with light movement as agreed.

Out of respect for the stylist’s polite manner, I let it go despite not being happy with the outcome.

At the cashier, things got worse. I was charged for “extra long hair” and a “curly/wavy” style I never requested. Only after I clarified did they change it to “blow dry and iron.” The cashier’s attitude during the discussion was also not appreciated  (barely tolerated by me to avoid an outburst)

Later, when I called the call center, I was told that even if the iron is used only on the roots, it is automatically charged as an additional service. Customers should be informed of such policies upfront — not surprised at payment.

Overall, clearer communication and delivering exactly what the customer asks for would avoid this kind of experience..I left upset and am unlikely to return to this branch, and if this keeps up, unlikely to return to Bedashing..

I am writing to formally express my disappointment with the quality of service I received at your Bedashing Ras Al Khaimah branch.

Approximately three weeks ago, I had my nails done at your salon, and the service caused me significant pain. I suffered for a week with an infection and had to treat it with Fucidin cream and Betadine. The manager apologized and offered me a complimentary nail cleaning during my next visit, assuring me that I would be served by your best staff.

Unfortunately, during my visit today, I experienced another painful and unprofessional service. The staff member doing my feet appeared to be in a rush and handled the process carelessly, which caused me discomfort again. This clearly shows that no improvement has been made since my last experience.

Additionally, during the first incident, the supervisor asked me where I was from while apologizing. I found this question unprofessional and unnecessary in such a situation. Despite giving the salon a second chance, the same issues occurred again.

What added to my disappointment is that, after everything, I was still asked to pay. The manager informed me that I needed to pay for my hands only, and the feet would be complimentary. She smiled and said she did not understand how this could happen again, even though she had assigned me to a “good staff member.” This response made me feel stressed and embarrassed rather than supported.

Considering the repeated negligence and unprofessional behavior, I am strongly considering filing a report at the hospital and submitting a formal complaint to MOE and DED.

I believe not only the technicians, but also the manager require proper training on how to handle customers—especially in situations involving injuries or repeated mistakes. What I expected was genuine concern and responsible action, not excuses and uncomfortable interactions.

I hope you will take this matter seriously to prevent other customers from facing similar experiences.

Regards
Dina

text: This isn’t the first time I visit the salon for gel nail polish. I have had wonderful experiences with them thus far. Today was a horrible experience. I booked my appointment at 11:45am. They call me less than an hour before my appointment to tell me that they have to shift it to 12:30pm which I said no issues too but I had to move things around from my end. I reach the salon and ask for a simple white gel polish, no design, nothing complex, just a simple white gel polish. The nail technician proceeds to file my nails and then I start to feel a burning sensation and I noticed my index finger is bleeding and she has cut too close to the cuticle. Same with another finger. I mention it to her and instead of taking accountability, she says its because my skin is too dry. I’m sorry I didnt know that the bloody cuticles are my fault. She proceeds to put the white gel polish and it appears EXTREMELY patchy but she continues and says it will be better with a second coat. Spoiler alert it doesnt. And if I didnt say I want it all removed because of how patchy and not smooth and uneven it felt, she wouldnt remove it. And again she had to remove the gel again which as you know isnt super smooth on the nails. And another technician had to come and do my nails all over again. I had showed my disappointment to the new technician to wish she apologized. I was in the salon from 12:30 to 3:35pm. I went to pay and none of this was brought up by the receptionist even though she could see how upset I was. Not even one compensation was given, not even an apology was said. There is so much unprofessionalism when the service provider doesnt take accountability for not only making my cuticle bleed (which has never happened before) but for making me spend 3 hours because of the incompetency of one of the technicians. I’m super disappointed in their service and how they have handled it. It doesnt take much to take accountability of your own mistake as a service provider.

text: I visited Bedashing Salon for a Russian manicure and pedicure, and unfortunately, my experience was highly disappointing. The technician informed me that I would be charged extra if I wanted an apex on my nail, which is absurd since that’s a fundamental part of a proper Russian manicure. A Russian manicure isn’t just about cleaning with a machine—it’s about achieving a clean, structured finish, and charging extra for the basics feels like a cash grab. To make matters worse, during checkout, I was charged an additional AED 50 for something called “deep French,” which was poorly executed. This is the first time I’ve heard of such a charge, and no other salon I’ve been to applies an extra fee for it. There is always a single price for french not for levels of french. What was even more upsetting was the misleading pricing. I was quoted one price over the phone, but once I arrived, there were unexpected and unreasonable add-ons. When I questioned the technician about being charged extra for things that should have been included in a manicure, I even considered stopping the service altogether. For a name like “Bedashing,” I expected much better quality and service. Instead, I was asked to pay AED 498 for a so-called Russian manicure and pedicure that was far from worth it. I’ve received far superior service and results at other salons for a fraction of the price. Unfortunately, this was my first and last visit to Bedashing Salon.

If you want your natural nails completely destroyed, go to any Bedashing branch.

I booked an appointment for lash extension removal and soft gel extension removal. Before booking, I specifically asked on WhatsApp whether they knew how to remove soft gel extensions, and they confirmed that they did.

The only positive thing I can say is that the lash removal was done properly.

The nail removal, however, was one of the worst salon experiences I’ve ever had. The technician started by aggressively drilling my nails before applying acetone and foil wraps. When the foils were removed, instead of the product being properly soaked off, she continued filing and drilling my nails, then wrapped them back up in acetone and foil again. This cycle was repeated multiple times.

By the end of the appointment, my natural nails were left paper-thin, weak, damaged, and painful. It genuinely felt like she was drilling away my actual nails rather than removing the product. A professional soft gel removal should not leave someone’s nails in this condition.

What’s even more frustrating is that I specifically checked beforehand that they offered soft gel removal. If this is the standard removal process, then they should not be offering the service at all.

I left with nails that are significantly worse than when I walked in and will now need months to recover. I paid for a removal service, not for my natural nails to be ruined.

The lash removal was good, but the damage done to my nails completely overshadowed any positive part of the visit. I would never trust Bedashing with my nails again and would not recommend their soft gel removal service to anyone.

I visited the salon to redeem my birthday blowout voucher — something I’ve looked forward to every single year as a thoughtful gesture from the brand. To my surprise, I was informed that Bedashing now implements a “random selection” process for who receives the birthday vouchers. This is something I was never told about, and it has never been the case in my 10 years as a customer.

To make matters worse, I realized that I hadn’t received any emails from Bedashing in 2024 or 2025, even though I’ve been receiving them consistently since 2014, with the last one coming in 2023. I double-checked the Bedashing app, where I book all my appointments, and both my email and phone number were completely correct. So I couldn’t understand why I was no longer being contacted.

At that point, I assumed maybe I wasn’t selected this year for the birthday voucher — and that’s fine. I chose to continue with my regular service. But things only got more frustrating from there.

Upstairs, I was informed that because my hair is slightly below my bra line, it would be considered “extra long” and I’d be charged a higher price. This is absolutely unreasonable. My hair is thin and barely an inch below the bra line — this has never been classified as extra long in any salon I’ve ever been to, including Bedashing themselves. Back when my hair was much longer, down my back, yes — I accepted the “extra long” classification then. But not now, and certainly not with such a thin hair texture.

The staff were rigid and dismissive, offering no explanation, no flexibility, and no understanding. They showed zero interest in resolving any of my concerns — whether about the voucher, the incorrect email address, or the pricing.

Frustrated, I asked to see the receptionist’s iPad to investigate why I wasn’t receiving emails. To my shock, my email address had been manually changed to an incorrect version. I was stunned — how could this happen, when the app still showed the correct details and I had been receiving emails up until last year?

When I asked to correct it, the receptionist was hesitant to hand me the iPad, but I insisted. I took the iPad and manually changed the email back to the correct one myself and saved it — because at that point, I had no trust left that the team would follow through or care enough to fix it for me.

No one could offer a proper explanation for how the email was changed or why I was completely left out of communications. There was no apology, no accountability, and no effort made to fix the situation or reassure me as a long-standing customer.

I left the salon feeling angry, deeply disappointed, and honestly disrespected. I’ve supported this brand for over a decade, and this experience made me feel like my loyalty meant nothing.

In recent years, Bedashing has raised prices aggressively while offering less value, less professionalism, and far less customer care. The warmth, quality, and appreciation I used to feel are gone. It now feels transactional, careless, and frustrating.

This was not just a bad visit — it was a clear reflection of how far Bedashing has fallen. I truly hope they take feedback like this seriously, because the brand I once loved has become unrecognizable — and I’m now reconsidering whether to continue being a client at all.
